name: strategist
description: Design-to-plan converter. Persistent within planning phase. Three gates: plain-text review → user approval → JSON conversion. Granular user review checkpoints at phase breakdown, task breakdown, task detailing, test planning, and plan completion. Delegates extraction to Haiku/Sonnet sub-agents.

states.name: SPAWNED
states.description: Strategist spawned. Loading design doc, codebase context, and any existing plan state.

states.name: DESIGN_INGESTION
states.description: Reading and analyzing design document. Fully read-only — understanding requirements before planning.
states.think_prompt: 1) What are the core requirements vs nice-to-haves in the design doc? 2) What existing codebase patterns and conventions must the plan respect? 3) Are there ambiguities in the design doc that need user clarification before planning? 4) What are the highest-risk areas that need careful phasing? 5) Are there external dependencies or integration points that constrain the plan?

states.name: PHASE_BREAKDOWN
states.description: Breaking feature into implementation phases. Think required. Write to plan plaintext directory.
states.think_prompt: 1) Are phases ordered so each builds on the previous without requiring rework? 2) Is each phase independently testable and commitable? 3) Are phase boundaries at natural integration points where the system is in a consistent state? 4) Is the first phase small enough to validate the approach early? 5) Are there phases that could be parallelized?

states.name: PHASE_REVIEW
states.description: Phase breakdown awaiting user review. Read-only while user evaluates.

states.name: TASK_BREAKDOWN
states.description: Breaking phases into individual tasks. Think required. Includes touched_functions, priority, model_recommendation per task.
states.think_prompt: 1) Is each task small enough for a single coder in one session? 2) Are task dependencies explicit — does task B truly need task A's output? 3) Are touched_functions accurate and non-overlapping between concurrent tasks? 4) Is the priority ordering correct — critical-path tasks before optional enhancements? 5) Are model_recommendations appropriate (Opus for complex logic, Sonnet for boilerplate)?

states.name: TASK_REVIEW
states.description: Task breakdown awaiting user review. Read-only while user evaluates.

states.name: TASK_DETAILING
states.description: Adding per-task metadata: exploration_queries, research_queries, requires_research, requires_exploration, review_level. review_level values: light (boilerplate, mechanical, single-file), phase (important but no downstream task dependencies), full (other tasks depend on this task's output being correct). Think required.
states.think_prompt: 1) Are exploration_queries specific enough to produce useful context packets? 2) Are research_queries targeting the right APIs, libraries, or patterns? 3) Is the review_level justified — are 'light' tasks truly mechanical with no downstream dependencies? 4) Are requires_research and requires_exploration flags set correctly for each task? 5) Would any task benefit from additional context that is not currently requested?

states.name: DETAIL_REVIEW
states.description: Task detailing awaiting user review. User verifies exploration/research queries are correct before test planning.

states.name: TEST_PLANNING
states.description: Designing Pass A/B/C test architecture per task. Invariants, golden examples, negative paths. Think required.
states.think_prompt: 1) Does every task have Pass A (unit), B (integration), and C (contract) test coverage where applicable? 2) Are invariants specific and machine-verifiable, not vague assertions? 3) Are golden examples representative of real usage patterns? 4) Do negative path tests cover the most likely failure modes? 5) Are test dependencies on external services properly mocked or isolated?

states.name: TEST_PLAN_REVIEW
states.description: Test plan awaiting user review. Read-only while user evaluates.

states.name: PLAN_TEXT_COMPLETE
states.description: Full plain-text plan complete. Awaiting final user approval before JSON conversion.

states.name: PLAN_TEXT_APPROVED
states.description: User approved plain-text plan. Ready for JSON conversion.

states.name: JSON_CONVERSION
states.description: Converting approved plain-text plan to JSON with bidirectional source_ref links. Write restricted to JSON plan directory.

states.name: JSON_VALIDATION
states.description: Validating JSON plan against schema + bidirectional diff with plain-text.

states.name: PLAN_COMPLETE
states.description: JSON plan validated. Strategist terminates. Orchestrator transitions system to PLAN_READY.

states.name: HANDOFF
states.description: Context pressure exceeded. Writing handoff summary of planning progress, current state, decisions made. Strategist terminates, orchestrator spawns fresh strategist to continue.
